A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaViT research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original attention analyses on 1,000 Visual-CoT samples, LaViT benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and latent-token/training-step experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds inference-timing measurements, data-scaling experiments, and dataset-filtering statistics.

M1.justification: The latent-token procedure, semantic and trajectory losses, curriculum gating, and joint objective are retained. Top-K sparsification becomes Top-N with the same value of eight. Final-token-only supervision, newly emphasized in the main text, was already documented in v1 Appendix C.2; expanded filtering details do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix B.2 adds Jigsaw evaluation to the previously tested perception and spatial-reasoning tasks. The original benchmarks and the 14,567-example training corpus with ten source datasets remain; the new training-subset sizes do not introduce additional domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator roster. The added timing and scaling analyses reuse existing methods, including the base model, SFT, LVR, and DMLR. Implementing LVR at 3B for timing is a model-configuration difference, not a new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: The original main training settings remain. New supplementary protocols vary training data from 3K to 15K while fixing total iterations, and measure batch-one latency on all 300 MMVP samples with 3B LVR and DMLR implementations. Figure 2 also extends the reported focusing-threshold sweep from 20% to 30%.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands supporting analyses through controlled data-scaling experiments, a breakdown of inference costs, and analysis of source-dependent filtering acceptance. These examine data dependence, computational overhead, and selection effects absent from v1. Existing component and latent-token/checkpoint ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 adds box-and-whisker summaries of focusing scores for correct and incorrect samples, replacing the earlier count/mean display and adding descriptive spread information. Figure 3 retains error-bar reporting and Table 2 retains standard deviations and coefficients of variation. No repeated-run protocol or defined confidence intervals are added.

E6.justification: V2 adds data-scaling curves, latency measurements, and filtering outcomes. Table 5 reports total latency of 0.143 seconds for LaViT, 0.215 for LVR, and 1.177 for DMLR; Table 9 reports 30,500 candidates and 47.8% acceptance. Section 3.1 corrects its prose means from 15.89%/11.84% to 18.78%/9.18%, matching values already plotted in v1 Figure 2, while the revised figure adds higher-threshold results. Main Tables 1–3 and the existing token-count ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The focusing-score definition, attention aggregation, gating equations, losses, and gradient argument remain mathematically equivalent. Equation 2 expands notation and explanation; the new filtering pseudocode documents an existing operation. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the Perception Gap claim, attention-guided latent distillation contribution, curriculum-gating contribution, and claims of up to 16.9-point gains and competitiveness with larger models. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions attribute faster text decoding to reduced KV-cache burden, interpret SFT scaling behavior as overfitting, and explain weak low-data LaViT performance through limited generalization. They also relate filtering acceptance differences to alignment difficulty. Figure 2's caption modestly softens its necessity interpretation, although stronger causal language remains elsewhere.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information: the GPT-4o snapshot, VLMEvalKit, timing hardware and software, MiMo-V2-Flash correctness judge and prompt, Gemini-2.5-Flash difficulty filter, and stepwise bounding-box filtering pseudocode. It replaces the earlier GitHub access pointer with an anonymous repository and explicitly reports code, model, and dataset releases. These are newly documented details and access information, not evidence that the original experiments changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including ClueAegis, REVEAL, Driver-WM, MonoSR, VLMEvalKit, and MiMo-V2-Flash. These are limited additions to contextual and implementation references; the central positioning around dynamic attention-guided latent reasoning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained. Local revisions clarify the SFT control and attention extraction, distinguish Top-N sparsification from K latent tokens, and move ablation definitions from a caption into prose. Appendix headings expand and references move after the appendices.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figures 2 and 3 are redrawn, Tables 2 and 3 become adjacent, and new displays include the latency table, scaling figure, filtering algorithm, and filtering-statistics table. V1 Tables A1–A4 are retained as v2 Tables 4 and 6–8, rather than newly added evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility and assessability through fuller filtering/evaluation documentation, useful data-scaling and latency checks, and correction of the Section 3.1 text/figure inconsistency. Main benchmark and component-ablation results remain unchanged. The new efficiency interpretation needs qualification: Table 5 shows LaViT taking 0.143 seconds overall versus 0.062–0.063 for SFT/base, despite faster text decoding, and does not isolate the proposed KV-cache explanation.
